findings.title: `model` has no `(le` rule, so `modellen` and `modelleren` are wrongly split as compounds.
findings.body:
`snel`, `hotel` and `tabel` each get a higher-scoring `(le` rule for the inflection with a doubled consonant. `model` does not. In `modellen` (plural) and `modelleren` / `modellering`, what follows `model` is `l` plus a vowel, so `_) model (l@P5` matches. That rule emits `mo:d'E` and then translates the rest (`len`, `leren`) as a separate word. The result is roughly `mo:d'El,En` instead of `mo:d'El@n`: an extra stress and the wrong vowel in a common word, and `modelleren` loses its stress on `-le-`.

Fix: add `_) model (le      mo:d'El` before the `(l@P5` rule, as the sibling stems do.

findings.title: `huis` prefix rule stresses `huishoudelijk` on its first element.
findings.body:
`_) huis (C@P4` matches `huishoudelijk` and `huishoudelijke` (`h` plus a vowel follows), so the result is `h'Wysh,VUd@l@k`. The adjective is stressed on `-hou-` (huis**hou**delijk), like `hoofdzakelijk`, which this PR does add to `nl_list`. This is a common word.

Fix: add `huishoudelijk` and `huishoudelijke` to the `nl_list` exceptions.

findings.title: `levens` prefix rule moves the stress of `levenslang` onto `le-`.
findings.body:
`_) levens (C@P6` matches `levenslang`, giving `l'e:v@nsl,AN`. As an adjective or adverb ("hij kreeg levenslang"), the word is stressed on `lang`. The PR already treats `levensgevaarlijk` as a right-stressed exception, but `levenslang` is missing.

Fix: add `levenslang` and `levenslange` to `nl_list` with the stress on `lang`.

findings.title: `oor` prefix rule puts the primary stress of `oorspronkelijk` on `oor`.
findings.body:
`_) oor (C@P3` matches `oorspronkelijk`: after `oor` comes `s`, a consonant, and then a vowel. `oor` gets the primary stress and `spronkelijk` is translated as a separate word, giving `'O:rspr,ONk@l@k`. Standard stress is oor**spron**kelijk. This is the same `-lijk` pattern the PR already lists as exceptions (`hoofdzakelijk`, `klaarblijkelijk`), but this common word was left out.

Fix: add `oorspronkelijk` (and `oorspronkelijke`) to `nl_list` with stress on `spron`. I could not see what this word produced before the change.
